column7: ActivateBreakGlass inserted the activation record (state=active) and then granted the emergency role as two separate storage operations with no shared transaction and no lock, while RevokeBreakGlassActivationAtomic did its own pair under projectAdminGuardLockKey and deliberately TOLERATES ErrRoleNotAssigned ("already gone -- proceed to reconcile the record"). A revoke landing between the activation's two writes therefore removed nothing, transitioned the record to revoked, audited success, and the activation then granted the emergency role anyway. End state: a self-granted, SoD-bypassing role live for its full TTL while the record every reviewer and the UI reads says revoked -- and because the admin's revoke reported success nobody revisits it; ReconcileExpired only touches active rows so it never cleans it up; and the freed partial-unique-index slot lets the user activate a second time. Fixed by running the insert and the grant inside ONE acquisition of the SAME key the revoke takes, with the pair extracted into activateBreakGlassLocked so the two writes cannot be separated without the guard noticing; the audit and admin notification stay outside the lock, after the grant commits. NOT fixed with lockLiveParent, which is how every other fix in this class is built and which #2722's own suggested direction proposed: lockLiveParent requires the delete side to row-lock the PARENT before touching the children, and this revoke does the opposite (tx.RemoveRole runs BEFORE tx.RevokeBreakGlassActivation), so a FOR SHARE on the activation row would be read after the revoke had already looked for and not found the grant, and the race would survive the fix. Lock-order safety: one acquisition at family rank 3 with nothing nested inside, no inversion against storage.NamedLockOrder. This row is the structural default-ci guard, which also pins that the REVOKE still takes the same key -- dropping it there would silently reopen the race with nothing else going red. Red-proven by calling activateBreakGlassLocked without the lock: this guard fails, and so do both pg-gated tests (see break-glass-grant-survives-revoke-002)
